method: grep -rniE across site/ for api_key|apikey|authorization|bearer|token|secret|password|cookie|private_key|client_secret|AKIA|sk-<key-shaped>, plus full_text/fulltext/vault/internal_debug markers, each match read in context and manually classified.

high_risk_terms_api_key_bearer_client_se.note: Zero matches for api_key, apikey, bearer, client_secret, private_key, AKIA-style AWS key prefix, or sk-<20+ char> style key patterns anywhere under site/.

examples.file: site/news_global/*.html, site/data/*.json, site/tag/*.html, site/policy/6.html, site/home.html, site/talks/3.html
examples.match: secret / token / authorization appearing inside syndicated news headlines and article text
examples.reason: Editorial content: e.g. "NC's secret weapon for faster audits", "Destro AI's secret sauce", "agentic AI is breaking the token meter", "$150 Billion Share Repurchase Authorization Increase", "general secretary" (job title). These are quoted/aggregated news titles and summaries, not application secrets.

HTML <input type="password"> fields for a 4-digit editor PIN entry form. No literal password value, hash, or secret is present in the markup -- this is a UI input type attribute, not an exposed credential. The page is additionally the one path explicitly Disallow'd in site/robots.txt (Disallow: /editor/write.html).

findings.content: Operator Rights/Sources workbench pages, built by intel/operator_workspace/operator_ui.py and deployed as static HTML under site/operator/**.
findings.assessment: Reviewed against intel/operator_workspace/operator_boundary_contract.json, which is the project's own explicit, pre-existing design contract: 'Everything under site/ (including site/operator/**) is PUBLIC. No login exists on GitHub Pages.' The contract enumerates PUBLIC_SAFE_OPERATOR allowed_contents (report/claim/rights/source-health STATUS LABELS only, e.g. UNKNOWN_RIGHTS/UNKNOWN_ACCESS, never full text) versus forbidden_contents (full text, private notes, API keys/tokens/credentials, personal information) reserved for a NOT_IMPLEMENTED_THIS_PHASE PRIVATE_OPERATOR. Manual inspection of site/operator/rights/index.html and sources_full.json confirms only status labels and public source names/URLs are present -- no full text, no credentials, no personal information.
findings.classification: SAFE_TEXT (by design, per existing documented contract)
findings.note_not_a_new_finding: This is an intentional architectural decision already documented in the repo, not a gap introduced or discovered as a surprise. Flagged here for completeness/traceability only, not as a defect to fix.

internal_id_exposure_check.method: Spot-checked Public intelligence/report pages and the Operator rights page for internal-only identifiers.
internal_id_exposure_check.finding: Provenance IDs (document_id/evidence_id/claim_id/report_id, e.g. 'evt_a6a4027d9878143d') are shown on Public and Operator pages, but this is explicitly on the PUBLIC_SAFE_OPERATOR allowed_contents list ('Provenance IDs ... for cross-reference') and these IDs are opaque content-hash identifiers (see claim_model.py:_claim_id / hypothesis_model.py:_hypothesis_id, sha256-derived), not database primary keys, session tokens, or anything that grants access -- exposing them carries no security risk.

overall_result.summary: No credentials, API keys, tokens, passwords, cookies, or authorization headers were found literally present anywhere in site/. All 185 keyword matches for token/secret/password/authorization/cookie are editorial news content, a job title ('secretary'), a financial term ('Authorization Increase'), or HTML password-type input attributes with no embedded value. The one borderline area (site/operator/**) is a pre-existing, explicitly documented public-safe design, verified in this audit to actually comply with its own stated content boundary. No action required; nothing to rotate.
